title: Depression pay with Oliver and recording scale
summary: Oliver's men got $40 a week out of which they paid room and board; recording scale was $20 for four sides.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: We ought to talk a little bit about that period of the Depression. It seems that while there was certainly an economic depression, that the musicians seemed to do fairly well, that they worked and they made money from tips and from just the regular payment for jobs and so forth. When you were traveling with Oliver, that was really the beginning of the Depression. Did you experience any difficulties playing with Joe Oliver as far as the money was concerned?
Well, with King Oliver I think we got... We got a pretty fair price. We were getting forty dollars a week. Whether we worked three days or two days or five days or six
days, we still got that forty dollars. But we had our... Our room and board we had to pay out of that.
When we played recordings, the scale was very low during the recordings. When I recorded with King Oliver in 1929, or 1930 rather, scale was twenty dollars a session.
Yeah. I think that was four sides. Very low scale. It was very low.
